learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: Where does Euripides’ Medea begin?
Use the cited passage to explain: What distinguishes this play from the Argonautica?

main.work: The Tragedies of Euripides, Volume I
main.author: Euripides
main.locator: Medea, Nurse's opening account of Jason's new marriage; local text, normalized characters 290272-290495
main.excerpt: But now every thing is at variance, and the dearest ties are weakened. For having betrayed his own children, and my mistress, Jason reposes in royal wedlock, having married the daughter of Creon, who is prince of this land.

argo.author: Apollonius Rhodius
argo.locator: Argonautica 3, opening invocation; Book 3, normalized characters 0-476
argo.excerpt: Come now, Erato, stand by my side, and say next how Jason brought back the fleece to Iolcus aided by the love of Medea. For thou sharest the power of Cypris, and by thy love-cares dost charm unwedded maidens; wherefore to thee too is attached a name that tells of love. Thus the heroes, unobserved, were waiting in ambush amid the thick reed-beds; but Hera and Athena took note of them, and, apart from Zeus and the other immortals, entered a chamber and took counsel together
argo.note: Verbatim passage from Seaton's translation of Apollonius' Greek epic; it frames the quest as aided by Medea.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Apollonius frames the quest as a voyage for the fleece aided by Medea. Euripides begins later in Corinth, where the Nurse says Jason has married Creon's daughter while Medea is dishonored.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: The Nurse's speech recalls the Argo and Medea's earlier help, then turns to the new marriage and Jason's broken obligations.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Tragedy changes the question from how the fleece was won to what Jason owed the woman whose knowledge made him succeed.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: The Nurse’s wish that the Argo had never sailed is a character’s speech in a tragedy. It reframes a remembered expedition; it is not a statement by Apollonius about how his own epic should be read.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the clearest lesson in why a myth is never fully described by naming the hero.

quiz.prompt: What distinguishes this play from the Argonautica?

choices.text: It stages a later crisis rather than narrating the quest itself.
It is a handbook arranging the twelve labours.
It is a victory ode for Jason’s chariot race.
